```{r setup}
library(hyperion)
library(hyperion.tables)

project_dir <- system.file("extdata", "scm-vignette", package = "hyperion.tables")
options(hyperion.config_dir = project_dir)
scm <- read_scm(
  file.path(project_dir, "model", "nonmem", "PK", "scm", "scm-vignettescm.toml")
)
```

## SCM Lineage

An SCM summary table is a run summary table of the models a stepwise
covariate modeling (SCM) process fitted. The process here tested six
covariate effects on a two-compartment model, forward and then backward.
Start by loading its lineage tree, which `get_scm_lineage()` builds from
the process record:

```{r}
lineage <- get_scm_lineage(scm)

lineage
```

## Basic SCM Summary Table

`scm_summary_spec()` is the spec for an SCM summary table. It takes no
lineage: `apply_summary_spec()` gives it one, and the table gets a section
for each round the process ran:

```{r}
lineage |>
  apply_summary_spec(scm_summary_spec()) |>
  make_summary_table() |>
  render_to_image()
```

Each candidate's dOFV and p-value are against the model its round started
from. The working full and reduced covariate models are compared with the
base model, which this lineage lists under "Reference model". None of the
three is a candidate, so they have no description.

## Choosing Rounds

Use the `rounds` argument to control which rounds appear. Name the rounds
to show, here the first forward round:

```{r}
spec <- scm_summary_spec(rounds = "forward_round1")

lineage |>
  apply_summary_spec(spec) |>
  make_summary_table() |>
  render_to_image()
```

The base, working full and reduced covariate models always show.

## Marking the Selected Candidates

Use the `selected` argument to show which candidate each round selected.
It takes `ScmSelectedOptions()`; `column = TRUE` adds a Round Result
column:

```{r}
spec <- scm_summary_spec(
  rounds = "forward_round1",
  selected = ScmSelectedOptions(column = TRUE)
)

lineage |>
  apply_summary_spec(spec) |>
  make_summary_table() |>
  render_to_image()
```

`bold = TRUE` renders the selected candidate's row in bold:

```{r}
spec <- scm_summary_spec(
  rounds = "forward_round1",
  selected = ScmSelectedOptions(bold = TRUE)
)

lineage |>
  apply_summary_spec(spec) |>
  make_summary_table() |>
  render_to_image()
```

The two can be combined:

```{r}
spec <- scm_summary_spec(
  rounds = "forward_round1",
  selected = ScmSelectedOptions(column = TRUE, bold = TRUE)
)

lineage |>
  apply_summary_spec(spec) |>
  make_summary_table() |>
  render_to_image()
```

The same on every round:

```{r}
spec <- scm_summary_spec(
  selected = ScmSelectedOptions(column = TRUE, bold = TRUE)
)

lineage |>
  apply_summary_spec(spec) |>
  make_summary_table() |>
  render_to_image()
```

## Selected Candidates Only

`selected_only = TRUE` leaves out the candidates the rounds did not select.
The steps that remain are grouped under "Forward" and "Backward":

```{r}
spec <- scm_summary_spec(
  selected = ScmSelectedOptions(selected_only = TRUE)
)

lineage |>
  apply_summary_spec(spec) |>
  make_summary_table() |>
  render_to_image()
```

## Rounds by Direction

`rounds` also takes a direction, `"forward"` or `"backward"`, for every
round that ran in it:

```{r}
spec <- scm_summary_spec(rounds = "backward")

lineage |>
  apply_summary_spec(spec) |>
  make_summary_table() |>
  render_to_image()
```

## Descriptions

The Description column shows what each fit added or dropped.
`description = "verbose"` adds the covariates its model has:

```{r}
spec <- scm_summary_spec(
  description = "verbose",
  selected = ScmSelectedOptions(column = TRUE, bold = TRUE)
)

lineage |>
  apply_summary_spec(spec) |>
  make_summary_table() |>
  render_to_image()
```

With `selected_only = TRUE`, the verbose descriptions show the model
growing and shrinking step by step:

```{r}
spec <- scm_summary_spec(
  description = "verbose",
  selected = ScmSelectedOptions(selected_only = TRUE)
)

lineage |>
  apply_summary_spec(spec) |>
  make_summary_table() |>
  render_to_image()
```

The covariates come from the process record, so verbose descriptions need
the lineage from `get_scm_lineage()`.

## Table Title

```{r}
spec <- scm_summary_spec(
  title = "Forward Selection",
  rounds = "forward",
  selected = ScmSelectedOptions(selected_only = TRUE)
)

lineage |>
  apply_summary_spec(spec) |>
  make_summary_table() |>
  render_to_image()
```

## Summary Table Modifiers

An SCM summary spec is a `SummarySpec`, so the summary table modifiers
apply to it:

```{r}
spec <- scm_summary_spec(
  title = "Covariate Search",
  selected = ScmSelectedOptions(selected_only = TRUE)
) |>
  set_spec_columns("description", "ofv", "dofv", "pvalue") |>
  set_spec_pvalue(scientific = TRUE)

lineage |>
  apply_summary_spec(spec) |>
  make_summary_table() |>
  render_to_image()
```
